frontier.hypothesis: The `sll $a0` / `sll $v0`+`addu` transposition is decided at RTL emission (expand / sched1 luid order), not by any C statement arrangement, and the dumps will name the pass in one read.
frontier.mechanism: s50 measured statement order, chain shape, deref shape and typing all inert at 2 across 440 compiles, which is the signature of a decision taken before the C-visible order matters. With priorities tied, sched.c:2463 rank_for_schedule falls through to INSN_LUID(y) - INSN_LUID(x) and prefers the higher luid; luid is the post-expand order, so the question is which sll gets the higher luid at expand.
frontier.next_probe: Apply memory/grind/CD_datasync/candidate.c, run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 CD_datasync`, and read tmp/grind/CD_datasync/dumps/*.rtl (expand order of the two sll insns relative to arg5's addu) and *.sched (block-3 dependence graph + PICK trace under BB2_SCHED_DEBUG=1). frontier.hypothesis: The remaining transposition is an allocation-order artefact reachable from ra_solver's local-alloc model, now that the register ASSIGNMENT matches target exactly and only one insn's position differs.
